title: University of Maryland - CS10

question.stem: Select the 3 findings that are most concerning.

options.text: Positive motion of R lower extremity
2+ pedal edema
Pain 8/10 in right calf
Warmth noted to right calf
Right pedal pulse 2+
Right lower extremity elevated
Blood pressure 145/82 mm Hg
HR 96 beats/min
Positive sensation of R lower extremity

question.footnote: Taken from the Maryland Next Gen NCLEX Test Bank Project, University of Maryland School of Nursing: “Deep Vein Thrombosis II” medical-surgical faculty case study (Dawn Leukhardt, MSN, RN, College of Southern Maryland, La Plata, Maryland, September 1, 2022). Available at https://www.nursing.umaryland.edu/mnwc/initiatives/nextgen-nclex/nextgen-nclex-library/ (Faculty Case Studies).
question.explanation:
The nurse should recognize signs of a possible deep vein thrombosis: pedal edema, calf pain, and warmth of the right calf. The pedal pulse is normal: DVT obstructs a vein, so it does not usually weaken the arterial pulse.
Positive motion and sensation are expected and not concerning. The blood pressure and heart rate are borderline, likely related to the pain, and not a primary concern. The elevation of the extremity and the bedrest order must be followed but are not concerning findings about the client’s condition.

question.explanation:
Edema and pain are consistent with all three problems. Warmth of the calf may be seen with infection and DVT.
Fever suggests infection. A DVT does not usually decrease the pedal pulse, because it blocks a vein, not an artery. Limited range of motion is consistent with a soft tissue injury, but not with DVT.

question.footnote: Taken from the Maryland Next Gen NCLEX Test Bank Project, University of Maryland School of Nursing: “Deep Vein Thrombosis II” medical-surgical faculty case study (Dawn Leukhardt, MSN, RN, College of Southern Maryland, La Plata, Maryland, September 1, 2022). question.preamble: The nurse has reviewed the Nurses’ Notes from Day 1 1010 with the radiology results.
question.explanation: The nurse should anticipate anticoagulation therapy, which may include an initial bolus dose of heparin followed by a continuous infusion; heparin requires a baseline PTT and monitoring of the PTT every 6 hours per protocol. Elevation of the right lower extremity is indicated. Current guidelines support walking as tolerated once anticoagulation has started; it does not increase the risk of pulmonary embolism. A sequential compression device is not applied to a leg with an acute DVT, because squeezing the leg could dislodge the thrombus. Massage is contraindicated because it can dislodge the thrombus.

question.preamble: The nurse has reviewed the Nurses’ Notes from Day 1 1018 and the Orders.
question.explanation:
The PT/PTT should be drawn immediately because it is a STAT order and the heparin cannot be started until it is done. Bedrest is implemented immediately, as ordered, and the client is weighed right away because the heparin bolus and infusion are dosed by weight.
The heparin bolus and the initial infusion should begin within the hour to prevent extension of the DVT, and monitoring for bleeding begins with the bolus. The right leg should be elevated soon, but it is not the first priority.
The PTT is redrawn 6 hours after the infusion starts, per the orders.

question.stem: Which client statements indicate the teaching was understood? Select all that apply.

options.text: “To relieve my stress, I should have a glass of wine before dinner.”
“I will eat more spinach and kale every day.”
“I will throw away my straight razor and buy an electric one.”
“If I miss a dose of my medicine, I will contact my doctor.”
“Controlling my blood pressure is not important.”
“When I travel, I will get out and walk every 3–4 hours.”
“I set an alarm so I take my medicine at the same time daily.”

question.preamble: The nurse has reviewed the Day 3 Orders and the Progress Notes. The client is reassessed on the third day, and discharge orders are received.
question.explanation:
Because of the bleeding risk, the client should use an electric razor. Warfarin is taken at the same time every day, so the client should contact the provider for instructions if a dose is missed.
Alcohol should be avoided because it increases the effect of warfarin and the risk of bleeding. Green leafy vegetables contain vitamin K, which can decrease the effect of warfarin, so the intake should stay consistent rather than increase. The client should maintain a healthy weight and control blood pressure to reduce the risk of another DVT, and when traveling should get up and walk every 1–2 hours.
